story.title: Story 4: Smart Compact Snapshot And Rollout Regeneration

result.planSummary: Implemented SQLite-backed compact snapshot reads, removed mixed post-build smart-compact reads, tightened projection metadata persistence/error handling, and added SQLite story coverage for strict, prepare, and regeneration flows.

changedFiles.reason: Added the compact snapshot contract to the shared store interface.
Provided a compatibility `readCompactSnapshot` implementation for legacy file-backed callers.
Added transactional `readCompactSnapshot` support and reused shared projection/chunk readers for consistent SQLite snapshot loads.
Switched projection builds to consume one compact snapshot instead of split thread/chunk reads and surfaced snapshot thread metadata/read revision in results.
Used snapshot-thread metadata for generated output/counting, removed premature generated identity mapping, and now fail explicitly when projection metadata persistence fails.
Added reusable SQLite smart-compact fixture/counter helpers for story coverage.
Added SQLite smart-compact coverage for consistent snapshot source revision behavior and source-vs-projection truth.
Added SQLite prepare-mode coverage proving strict blockers remain until explicit prepare catch-up runs.
Added SQLite rollout regeneration coverage for missing generated-output recovery and metadata refresh.

gatesRun.command: node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "fixture creation command|creates a valid thread-shaped fixture" tests/context-steward/e2e-cli.e2e.test.ts

node --import tsx --test --test-name-pattern "^real PI execution continues the same prepared long-thread clone session with a second closed turn$" tests/context-steward/long-thread-real-pi-execution.e2e.test.ts

findingsFixed: Smart compact no longer builds from split thread/chunk reads and now uses a single store-level compact snapshot contract.
Final generated-session counting and PI file creation now use the same compact snapshot thread metadata instead of reopening the thread after build.
Projection metadata persistence is now checked explicitly, and the command no longer records generated-session identity mappings before metadata commit succeeds.
findingsSurfaced: `npm run verify-all` is still unstable because long-running PI E2E coverage can time out inside the full suite even when the same failing test passes on isolated rerun.

result.recommendedNextStep: Stabilize or re-run the flaky full-suite long-thread E2E timeout so `npm run verify-all` goes green, then hand Story 4 to verification.
